summary:
The SP category is the story of the week — R1 and R2 both sit at 59-60% over the last 14 days (n=102) versus a season baseline of 53%, both flagged HOT at +5.9pts. That's not noise at this sample size, and it lines up cleanly with today's board: all four games feature clear SP-driven splits, with Luzardo/Sale and Tolle/Schlittler as the marquee arms. R3's hot category has flipped to runs (60%, +5.9pts) and hitting (55%, +5.9pts) instead of SP, which matters because R3 is also the model that just posted a 30-13 (70%) strong-play stretch over the last 14 days — best of any rating. R4 is right behind it at 27-13 (68%, +21.0u) over the same window, riding a hot runs category (60%, +5.5pts) that's roughly double its season average delta. All four ratings carry active 3-4 game winning streaks in trends, and trends+sp remains the best category combo on the board all year at 57.8% (355-259, n=614) — worth noting since three of today's four games have full 4-rating consensus.

On the slate itself, PHI @ ATL and BOS @ NYY are the plays where the hot categories actually converge with the picks: ATL gets the largest R4 delta of the day (+1.07) backed by a real pitching mismatch (Sale vs Luzardo), and NYY's Schlittler start pushes R4 to its single biggest number of the day (+1.29) in a game where all four ratings agree. CHC @ SDP is a clean 4-way consensus too, but Boyd is a soft matchup against King, so lean on the hot SP signal cautiously if backing CHC. The one to fade or treat lightly is CHW @ HOU — every rating leans CHW, but the deltas are small and negative in direction relative to typical winning consensus strength (R1 -0.32, R4 -0.18), and CHW carries none of the team-when-liked support that MIL, TBR, BOS, and LAD show (all 65%+ with strong positive units). If forced to rank confidence, go ATL and NYY first on the strength of the SP hot streak and full rating agreement, SDP second, and treat CHW as the lowest-conviction consensus of the four.
